name: Colorado
note: Colorado registers deaths through a statutory electronic death registration system: the funeral director who first takes custody files within 72 hours, and the physician, PA or APRN (or the coroner, for the deaths listed in § 30-10-606) completes the medical certification in the same system. No body may be buried, cremated or removed from the state without a disposition authorisation from the local vital statistics office or coroner. From the state registrar, deaths flow monthly to the secretary of state for voter cancellation and, on request, to the property tax administrator to stop senior and disabled-veteran exemptions. Certified copies require a direct and tangible interest; a short 'verification of death' document can substitute for the certificate.

citations.title: Determination of death
citations.quote: The individual has sustained irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions

citations.title: Coroner — inquiry — grounds
citations.quote: The responding law enforcement agency shall notify the coroner when a death is discovered or confirmed

citations.title: Coroner — inquiry where no physician can certify
citations.quote: When no physician is in attendance or when, though in attendance, the physician is unable to certify the cause of death

citations.title: Certificates of death — filing
citations.quote: A certificate of death for each death, including a stillborn death, that occurs in Colorado must be filed with the state registrar

citations.title: Certificates of death — electronic death registration system
citations.quote: The department of public health and environment shall create and the state registrar shall use an electronic death registration system

citations.title: Certificates of death — funeral director's duty to file
citations.quote: The funeral director or individual assisting in a nonprofessional capacity who first assumes custody of a dead body

citations.title: Certificates of death — medical certification
citations.quote: shall complete the medical certification for the certificate of death within seventy-two hours after receipt of the electronic death registration request

citations.title: Certificates of death — coroner's certification
citations.quote: the coroner shall determine the cause of death and shall complete and sign the medical certification within forty-eight hours

citations.title: Verification of death document
citations.quote: a verification of death document may be used by local offices of vital statistics and the state registrar when verifying a vital event

citations.title: Dead bodies — disposition — removal from state
citations.quote: No body shall be buried, cremated, deposited in a vault or tomb, or otherwise disposed of

citations.title: Certified copies furnished — fee
citations.quote: furnish to any applicant having a direct and tangible interest in a vital statistics record a certified copy of any record registered

citations.title: Penalties
citations.quote: refuses or neglects to perform any of the duties imposed upon the person by this article 2 commits a petty offense

citations.title: Centralized registration system — statistical data
citations.quote: Federal, state, local, and other public or private agencies may, upon request, be furnished copies of records of data for statistical purposes

citations.title: Centralized registration system — property tax exemption death matching
citations.quote: the state registrar shall identify all individuals on the list who have died and transmit a list of the names and social security numbers

citations.title: Deceased electors — monthly report
citations.quote: the state registrar of vital statistics shall furnish the secretary of state with a report of all persons eighteen years of age or older

citations.title: Deceased electors — cancellation
citations.quote: The county clerk and recorder shall cancel the registration of any elector who is deceased

citations.title: Deceased electors — family notice
citations.quote: The written notice shall be signed by a family member of the deceased.

citations.title: Computerized statewide voter registration list — death records
citations.quote: The secretary of state shall coordinate the computerized statewide voter registration list with state agency records on death.

steps.title: Determination of death under accepted medical standards
steps.who: A physician or other practitioner; the statute sets criteria rather than naming who pronounces.
steps.summary: An individual is dead on irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions or of all brain functions, in accordance with accepted medical standards.

steps.title: Police notify the coroner; coroner inquires into listed deaths
steps.who: The responding law enforcement agency; the coroner then notifies the district attorney.
steps.trigger: A death discovered or confirmed by police, or one of the listed circumstances (unnatural, intoxication, accident, unexplained child death, no physician able to certify, within 24 hours of hospital admission, in custody, sudden, unidentifiable).
steps.summary: The coroner must inquire into the cause and manner of death in the listed circumstances and then certifies the cause instead of the attending clinician.

steps.title: Clinician completes the medical certification in the electronic system
steps.who: The physician, physician assistant or APRN in charge of care (or the primary care clinician in some natural deaths), or an associate, the institution's chief medical officer, or the autopsy physician.
steps.trigger: Receipt of the electronic death registration request from the funeral director.

deadline.text: within seventy-two hours after receipt of the electronic death registration request

steps.summary: Medical certification must be done in the electronic death registration system. Repeated or wilful lateness is unprofessional conduct for physicians and PAs and grounds for discipline for APRNs.

steps.title: Coroner certifies cause where an inquiry is required
steps.who: The coroner (or medical examiner, forensic pathologist).

deadline.text: within forty-eight hours after receipt of the electronic death registration request, unless more time is needed

steps.summary: The coroner completes the medical certification electronically; if more time is needed, disposition waits for authorisation.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate electronically
steps.who: The funeral director, or a person assisting in a nonprofessional capacity, who first takes custody of the body; personal data come from the next of kin or best qualified source.

deadline.text: within seventy-two hours of assuming custody and prior to final disposition

steps.summary: The certificate is filed with the state registrar through the statutory electronic death registration system; deadlines extend over weekend and holiday closures. Neglecting a duty under article 2 is a petty offence.

steps.title: Authorisation for final disposition
steps.who: The county vital statistics office designated under § 25-2-103, or the coroner where none exists.
steps.trigger: Request by the custodian of the body before disposition.
steps.summary: No body may be buried, cremated, entombed or taken out of the state without this authorisation; cemeteries may not inter without it.

steps.title: Certified copies to those with a direct and tangible interest
steps.who: Any applicant with a direct and tangible interest, from the state registrar or a local vital statistics office.
steps.summary: Vital records are confidential. A shorter 'verification of death' document (no SSN) may be issued and counts as a death certificate wherever the statutes use that term.

steps.title: State registrar reports deceased adults to the secretary of state monthly
steps.who: The state registrar of vital statistics, for persons 18 or older, with name, county, date of birth and SSN where possible.

deadline.text: as soon as practicable after the end of each month

steps.summary: The secretary of state coordinates the statewide voter list with state death records and may cancel deceased registrations electronically.

steps.title: Secretary of state forwards deaths to county clerks, who cancel
steps.who: The secretary of state, to each county clerk and recorder.
steps.trigger: The monthly report from the state registrar.
steps.summary: County clerks must cancel the registration of deceased electors notified this way.

steps.title: Family member's written notice cancels a registration
steps.who: A family member of the deceased, to the county clerk and recorder.
steps.summary: The clerk cancels on signed family notice, or without it on sufficient proof.

steps.title: Registrar flags deceased property-tax exemption holders
steps.who: The state registrar, to the property tax administrator (Division of Property Taxation).
steps.trigger: Receipt of the administrator's list of senior and disabled-veteran exemption holders, and qualified-senior primary residences.
steps.summary: Notwithstanding vital records confidentiality, the registrar matches the list against deaths and returns names and SSNs of those who have died.

steps.title: Death data for statistical purposes
steps.who: Federal, state, local and other public or private agencies, on terms set by regulation.
steps.summary: The registrar may furnish copies of records or data for statistical purposes and publishes annual vital statistics reports.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: 72 hours from the funeral director assuming custody (not from death), before disposition; extended for weekend/holiday closures.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director (or nonprofessional custodian) who first takes custody files; next of kin supply personal data.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of every certificate; the coroner certifies only deaths requiring inquiry under § 30-10-606.

electronicRegistration.note: Statute requires the state registrar to use an electronic death registration system and requires certifiers and coroners to certify in it.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the state registrar keeps a centralized vital statistics registry and pushes deaths only where statutes direct.

governmentPropagation.note: Registration automatically reaches the voter roll monthly, and the property tax administrator by list matching. No statutory death feed to the Division of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue income tax, or Health Care Policy and Financing was found. Federal feeds are in us-federal.

certificateAccess.note: Vital records are confidential; certified copies only to an applicant with a direct and tangible interest.

gaps: privateSectorVerification is left to the us-federal layer (LADMF); no Colorado statute giving banks or insurers a verification route was found.
The Colorado Board of Health rules (5 CCR 1006-1) defining 'direct and tangible interest' were not read; the CCR host was not tried.
No statute requiring the Division of Motor Vehicles to cancel a deceased person's licence on notice from vital records was found in Title 42 (searched for 'vital statistics', 'deceased', 'decedent').
Title 25.5 (Medicaid) and Title 39 income tax were not searched for death feeds.
Whether Colorado's EDRS transmits to SSA is not stated in the statutes read; the federal side belongs in us-federal.
